text:
maria: Heads up — nightly autotune found a regression for some ROcm paths. Llama2-13b, seq=2048, tail p99 latency +15% when routed to rocm pool.

jake: Can you paste the profiler output?

maria: Sure. Short logs below (trimmed). Looks like a kernel availability mismatch triggers a slow fallback at a few operator shapes: 

```
# ./autotune --model llama2-13b --provider rocm --seq 2048 --profile
ROCM kernel lookup: matmul_tile_128x64 -> OK
ROCM kernel lookup: aten_matmul_small_tile_64 -> MISSING
fallback: use generic_matmul (cpuish, slow)
op=matmul shape=(64,64) -> chosen kernel=generic_matmul (4.3ms)
op=matmul shape=(128,64) -> chosen kernel=matmul_tile_128x64 (0.9ms)
Total step time: 22.1ms (expected ~19.2ms)
p99: 38.7ms (was 33.5ms)
```

maria: Note the missing op is "aten_matmul_small_tile_64" which we do ship for CUDA but not for several ROCm combos (rocm4.5 + gfx1030 fallback).

priya: Is this a compile-time missing kernel (we never built that tile size) or a signature mismatch?

maria: Looks like build missing. Kernel library doesn't include that small-tile specialization for fp16 int8 paths on gfx1030. Autotune falls back to generic implementation.

anita: Oof. This explains why some requests show a sudden latency jump after KV cache grows — shape of matmul changes once prefix tokens + response length > 1024, small-tile kernels are needed.

ken: So conditional routing currently just checks model version + device type and sends to rocm if pool available. We don't probe per-shape kernel availability. That makes sense as a cause.

oliver: Probing every request would be expensive. But we can do a cheap per-model+seq probe at routing time and cache the result. E.g. probe key=(model, seq, dtype, device_arch). Cache TTL like 1h.

maria: I ran an experiment: added a naive probe that runs the kernel lookup (no actual execution) and cached results. p99 improved back to baseline for the sample traffic. Implementation note: probe calls our kernel registry API: `registry.has_kernel(op, shape_hash, dtype, arch)`.

jake: Can you share the probe command?

maria: `curl -s -X POST http://runtime.local:8080/_probe_kernel -d '{"model":"llama2-13b","seq":2048,"arch":"gfx1030","dtype":"fp16"}'` returns `{"missing":["aten_matmul_small_tile_64"]}`

priya: Nice. Two follow-ups: 1) do we want to route to CUDA for sequences where ROCm misses important kernels? 2) Or prefer building the missing kernels in the ROCm build farm?

anita: For immediate mitigation, routing rule seems safest. But we should avoid blanket seq>1024 -> cuda heuristics; that's too coarse and breaks cost targets.

ken: Agreed. Proposed policy: conditional route when probe indicates one or more critical kernels missing AND estimated perf delta > X%. The runtime can estimate perf delta using a small lookup table from autotune runs.

maria: I attached a quick profiling matrix I produced offline (numbers are median ms per op):

```
shape     | rocm (ms) | cuda (ms)
(64,64)   | 4.3       | 1.1
(128,64)  | 0.9       | 0.8
(256,64)  | 0.7       | 0.6
step avg  | 22.1      | 19.1
```

maria: So if the missing kernel hits the hot path we get ~15% step regression which cascades at p99.

oliver: Implementation notes: we need three pieces: 1) a small registry probe endpoint in runtime, 2) a per-shape cache keyed by (model, seq, arch, dtype), 3) a routing decision function that takes cached probe result + perf delta threshold.

infra-bot: build-job queued: rocm-kernel-build/gfx1030/specialized-tiles #4721

ken: Ops. Good. That should address long-term. But the build queue is 2 hours for large kernel sets.

priya: Short-term patch plan: add probe + cached routing logic behind a feature flag `rocm_shape_probe_routing`. Canary the change to 5% of rocm pool.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: feature=rocm_shape_probe_routing, shard=canary-5pct, started_by=ken

maria: I'll prepare a small PR for runtime. It will: add endpoint, add LRU cache, add simple scoring: if missing_kernels includes >0 critical ops and estimated_drop>10% -> route to cuda.

anita: Also add a telemetry counter for "probe_missing_kernels" and "probe_routed_to_cuda" so we can quantify.

ken: Action items: 
1) infra: prioritize kernel build for gfx1030 small-tile set (follow infra-bot job).
2) runtime: maria + oliver to land probe+cache behind flag.
3) product/ops: agree on perf threshold and rollout plan.

maria: I'll open the PR and a short runbook for oncall: how to disable the feature flag if we see regressions.

jake: Thanks. This clarifies the root cause. Nice find. :thumbsup:

anita: +1. Let's avoid sweeping seq-based rules. Shape-aware routing is better. :+1:

deploy-bot: Canary 5% completed: no errors observed in 30m.

maria: Will monitor p99 for next 24h and report back here.

oliver: If cache TTL is too long we might miss a kernel rollout. Make TTL configurable and expire when we detect a kernel-build event for that arch.

infra-bot: build-job completed: rocm-kernel-build/gfx1030/specialized-tiles #4721 SUCCESS

maria: Nice. Once infra publishes artifacts we'll remove route-to-cuda override for affected model groups.

ken: Thanks all. I'll track progress and coordinate with SRE for canary metrics.

maria: Filing follow-ups: PR #3012 (runtime probe), infra job #4721 (kernel build), dashboard ticket #894 (probe telemetry).

oliver: cc @priya for rollout policy sign-off.

priya: Ack.

maria: End of thread.
